subject: Intermittent latency spike impacting checkout - evidence request and postmortem
messages:
From: Jamie Ortiz <jamie.ortiz@clearmart.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 30 Apr 2029 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent high-latency impacting checkout - possible SLA breach

Hi Rafael,

We observed a sustained latency spike starting 2029-04-30T07:45:00Z affecting checkout tokenization and confirmation for ~75% of requests in US-WEST-2. Our telemetry shows 95th percentile latency climbed from ~120ms to 2.1s and we saw ~40% failed confirmations for a 26-minute window before partial recovery. This impacted our peak morning batch and drove an outage for a subset of customers.

Can you confirm whether this window is eligible under the Redwood Availability SLA and what evidence you need from our side? I'm attaching a small sample of our logs (performance-sample-logs.zip) with request ids and timestamps.

We need an initial read — will this be escalated to an official SLA claim and postmortem? Please advise next steps and estimated timeline for an RCA.

Thanks,
Jamie Ortiz
Ops Lead, Clearmart
ops@clearmart.com

Attachment: performance-sample-logs.zip (zip)
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Ortiz <jamie.ortiz@clearmart.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Apr 2029 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent high-latency impacting checkout - possible SLA breach

Jamie — thanks for the heads up and for sending the sample. We've opened an internal ticket and will prioritize evidence collection. High-level next steps:

- Internal triage to confirm the exact impacted window and severity level
- Pull raw traces, routing logs, and autoscaler events for the timeframe you reported
- Evaluate eligibility against the Availability SLA (we'll check whether this meets the service outage definition vs. degraded latency)
- If eligible, we will scope any credit and provide a timeline for a postmortem (RCAs usually delivered within 10 business days for escalations)

Can you confirm two example request IDs from your sample that we should prioritize for trace-level correlation? Also confirm whether the users affected were all behind the same regional endpoint or spread across multiple subnets.

I'll keep you updated; Karthik and Soojin are looped in to pull the telemetry and run an initial impact assessment.

—Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Jamie Ortiz <jamie.ortiz@clearmart.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 May 2029 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent high-latency impacting checkout - possible SLA breach

Jamie / Rafael — quick internal update from infra after correlating host traces and autoscaler logs.

What we found so far (preliminary):
- Impact window: 2029-04-30T07:46:00Z to 2029-04-30T08:12:00Z (26 minutes)
- Root cause hypothesis: a temporary KV cache eviction cascade during a short burst of long-context requests caused sustained tokenization latency; autoscaler reacted but there was a delayed warmup on a subset of GPU-backed pods
- Affected customers: primarily US-WEST-2 checkout traffic routed through the shared inference pool; not global

Prelim SLA guidance: If the window meets the Availability definition (service unavailable or latency beyond the contractual SLO for sustained period), Clearmart is likely eligible for a proportional credit. We still need to:

1) Correlate the exact request IDs you provided against our internal request traces (please confirm the two IDs you want us to use for deep trace).
2) Pull the raw shard-level telemetry and top-level traces (we've attached the raw ingest traces we pulled: ingest-traces-20290430.tar.gz).

Estimate for a full RC A and credit calc: 7 business days from confirmation of the full request set and any additional log bundles you can provide. For now, we estimate a preliminary credit ballpark of ~3% of the affected day's monthly invoice (final amount pending full verification).

Let me know the two request IDs and whether you want us to proceed with an official SLA claim (we will file the claim and keep a running evidence bundle in INF-1024).

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Reliability, Redwood Inference
Attachment: ingest-traces-20290430.tar.gz (tar.gz)
From: Jamie Ortiz <jamie.ortiz@clearmart.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 02 May 2029 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent high-latency impacting checkout - possible SLA breach

Thanks Karthik — appreciate the quick triage.

Confirming two request ids from our sample for deep correlation: rc_20290430_214512 and rc_20290430_214679. Both are included in the performance-sample-logs.zip we attached earlier.

Please proceed with filing an official SLA claim and the postmortem. We agree to the proposed evidence timeline; Clearmart would like the postmortem and credit calc delivered as soon as available — ideally within the 7 business day estimate. Also please include the customer-facing summary of mitigations you plan to implement and any changes to autoscaling/warmup behavior so we can plan our mitigations as well.

Regards,
Jamie Ortiz
Ops Lead, Clearmart
